PROSE:
Rhea stood cornered at the rusted deposit node, caught between Vex's glowing holographic threats and Artie's desperate demands. She tightened her grip on her Makeshift Masonry Bludgeon, the heavy stone weight grounding her as the holographic clerk's blue light washed over the ash-covered clearing. On her right, the digitized avatar of Vex flickered with bureaucratic indignation, projecting a wall of scrolling red text into the stagnant air. On her left, Artie wheezed, his broken left arm cradled against a heavily bruised purple chest, looking like he was one stiff breeze away from expiring.

"You have incurred a Category Four UI Violation," Vex droned, his voice a perfectly modulated synthetic hum that managed to convey profound exhaustion. A glaring red banner hung in the air directly above his translucent, azure head. 

[System Audit Flag: Pending Administrative Review]

"The standard penalty for exploiting physics collisions to bypass the gathering tax is an immediate administrative ban," Vex continued, tapping a glowing clipboard that didn't actually exist. "I am required by protocol to quarantine your account, purge the anomalous ledger entries, and reset your physical form to the nearest respawn point. Which, given your current debt, is a sub-basement processing grinder."

"Don't you dare," Artie rasped, spitting a wad of bloody saliva onto the pale ash. His wild eyes locked onto the four Copper Credits clutched tightly in Rhea's left hand. "Tell me how you bypassed the stamina drain. Tell me right now. I'm dying here."

Rhea didn't move. She kept the Makeshift Masonry Bludgeon raised just enough to be a deterrent, her eyes flicking between the two of them. A small, clinical window hovered near Artie's shoulder, a stark reminder of the System's cruelty.

[Target: Artie]
[HP: 4/100]
[Status: Stage Two Systemic Shock, Minor Hemorrhage]

Rhea checked her own internal telemetry. She was sitting at twenty-five hit points and forty stamina. Better than Artie, but not nearly enough to survive a physical brawl with a desperate man, let alone whatever digital hell a system clerk could unleash. She couldn't fight them both. The math simply didn't support violence as a viable solution. 

"An audit means a regional supervisor has to look at your specific node, Vex," Rhea said, keeping her voice perfectly level. She let the words hang in the air, watching the clerk's digitized silhouette twitch. "They'll see that you left a physics loophole open. They'll see that you've been bleeding new arrivals dry with gathering taxes while simultaneously failing to secure the raw materials for the Overseer's quota. How much paperwork is a Category Four violation going to generate for you?"

Vex's azure light pulsed rapidly, the holographic threat stalling mid-scroll. The clipboard in his hands vanished, replaced by a gesture of pure, exasperated surrender. "The node's parameters are set by the Overseer. I merely enforce the ledger. Do you have any idea how many forms I have to file when a soul gets ground up in the sub-basement? It's seventeen pages. Front and back. In triplicate."

"And if the ledger balances, there's no anomaly," Rhea countered. She slowly lowered the Makeshift Masonry Bludgeon, letting its heavy, crude end rest gently against the ash. She didn't let go of the handle, but the aggressive posture melted into something resembling a business stance. "Artie needs untaxed resources to survive the hour. You need this audit flag to disappear without a trace so your boss doesn't delete you. I have the exploit that can solve both problems."

Artie coughed, a wet, rattling sound that made Rhea wince. "So what's the play? You gonna hold my hand and show me which rocks to hit?"

Rhea stepped toward the rusted terminal chassis of the deposit node. She reached out with her left hand, the cold metal of the Copper Credits pressing into her palm, and tapped the node's central crystal interface. "We form a party. A formal, System-recognized joint venture."

"A System party with a clerk?" Artie muttered, wincing as his chest heaved with another labored breath. "Is that even legal? He's a glowing blue hologram."

"It is a highly irregular gray area," Vex said, his tone shifting from authoritative to deeply calculating. He floated closer to the terminal, the blue light of his projection warring with the red glow of the pending audit flag. "If the party generates enough untaxed copper to cover the projected ledger deficit, the local system will classify the anomaly as a 'creative economic initiative' rather than a violation. The System respects profit above all things. But if you fail to meet the quota, the Overseer will notice, and I will be formatted."

"Then we don't fail," Rhea said. "Vex, you use your system access to bury the audit flag temporarily and classify our resource gathering as a sanctioned party operation. That gives us a localized tax exemption on shared actions. Artie, you provide the muscle and take the hits. I provide the methodology and manage the math."

"I have four hit points," Artie pointed out, gesturing weakly to his broken left arm. "I'm not exactly prime muscle."

"You heal when you level up, right?" Rhea asked, glancing at Vex for confirmation.

"Correct," Vex stated dryly. "A standard level-up fully restores HP and Stamina, though it does not mend durable injuries like fractures without specific restorative items."

"Good enough," Rhea said. She navigated the rusted terminal's glowing interface, pulling up the local group mechanics. The menus were dense, buried under layers of predatory legalese, but her brief experience with the System's contracts guided her fingers. With a sharp swipe, she projected a party interface window into the air between the three of them.

[Party Formation Request]
[Leader: Rhea]
[Members: Vex (Clerk), Artie (Indentured Soul)]
[Terms: Shared Ledger Liability, Equal Experience Distribution]
[Warning: Liability defaults to all active members upon failure.]

"Accept it," Rhea told Artie, her dark brown eyes locking onto his desperate gaze. "Or bleed out right here in the ash."

Artie didn't hesitate. He reached out with his good right hand, his bloody fingers trembling, and slammed his palm against the glowing blue 'Accept' rune. 

[Member Artie has joined the party.]

Vex stared at the floating holographic parchment for a long moment. "If this fails, the Overseer will dismantle my code line by line."

"If this fails, we're all dead anyway," Rhea said, her grip tightening on the handle of her weapon once more. "Tap the rune, Vex."

Vex sighed, a sound like static interference, and tapped the prompt. 

[Member Vex has joined the party.]
[Party Formation: Accepted]
[System Audit Flag: Suppressed]

The glaring red warning banner above Vex dissolved into a shower of harmless blue particles, fading into the ash. Rhea let out a breath she hadn't realized she was holding. The terminal chimed softly, registering the new systemic bond. They were officially bound together now—a dying man, a corrupt holographic bureaucrat, and a woman armed with a rock and four coins.
